records.region: Western Falcón, eastern approach to Embalse Matícora and Golfo de Venezuela; northeastern Zulia regional-map context
records.material_pending_reason: The chosen eastern opening and its initial tie into the visible north-trending upper branch are not completely covered by the inspected cartography. Regional basin and tributary prose cannot establish that missing connection.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Matícora is the eastern reservoir-bearing river in the inspected northeastern Zulia map. Cocuiza, eastern Palmar and Los Olivitos are distinct western features; their drainage descriptions do not resolve this selected Matícora approach.
records.completion_scope: Bounded research finished with supported upper visible branch, westward corridor, reservoir, lower river and actual gulf endpoint, plus an explicit eastern-opening material gap.
records.supported_name_scope: The named reservoir-outlet and lower gulfward receiving corridor are supported. The selected eastern opening remains unestablished; no uniform natural-river name is assigned across every feeder or reservoir passage.

scope_limits: One primary source-material-pending status covers the missing opening connection; this is not a completed naming-scope hold.
Riecito and Jordán occur in regional prose, but neither is assigned as the name of the unresolved selected opening.
The reservoir and gulf receiver are established at ordinary map/prose correspondence; exact present banks, flow, water level and dam operations are outside scope.
No formal registry, whole-feature scalar name or exact river-name transition has been verified.
The unavailable monograph supplies no map or substantive prose; a later inadvertently returned third-party snippet is excluded.

records.region: Camargo and Jiménez, southeastern Chihuahua; Bentín–Laguna de Palomas corridor
records.geographic_disambiguation: Representative identity for the connected selected Bentín drainage from the Sierra Agua de Mayo opening through Camargo and eastern Jiménez to the northern Laguna de Palomas receiving setting. Map labels read Bentín; the generic Arroyo describes the mapped intermittent watercourse.
records.completion_scope: Both municipal originals jointly establish all34selected parts, the opening, boundary transition, intermediate joins, lower corridor and actual northern Palomas receiving-flat terminal at ordinary regional/corridor scale.
records.supported_name_scope: Repeated Bentín mainstem labels and corresponding connected drainage. The name is not imposed on the receiving lake, every feeder or each headward vertex.

scope_limits: Formal name-registry status and precise legal hydronym scope remain unverified.
The opening is connected cartographically to Bentín; the representative identity does not make every headward portion an individually labeled reach.
Present water level, permanent discharge, salinity and local water-control operation were not established.
The optional DR0848 report has unknown HTTP/body after an actual status-action refusal and contributes no facts.

bounded_name_observations.name: Laguna de Palomas
bounded_name_observations.scope: Northern receiving-flat/inlet setting at the actual selected end; not a selected crossing of the entire lake.

records.region: Mapimí and western Tlahualilo, Durango, northern Mexico; the western Sierra Descubridora–Cerro Picacho de Ibarra feeder, El Barroso and the El Tordillo–Laguna Colorada–Las Liebres plain.
records.material_pending_reason: The particular southeastward selected connection from the El Tordillo stream corridor to Laguna Colorada. A source-established outlet or overflow/managed connection from Laguna Colorada through the selected southern and eastward plain loop. The actual final connection and inland terminal identity south of Las Liebres.
records.geographic_disambiguation: This selected inland system is not assigned the names Río Nazas, La Cadena, La India or Picoteria from neighboring mapped channels or basin labels. The stored end lies in the plain south of Las Liebres, not at the named Laguna de Tlahualilo, Laguna de Palomas or an ocean outlet.
records.completion_scope: All 25 selected parts in the one mainstem fragment were considered against two independently issued original municipal relief maps. The opening and northern named reach have ordinary corridor correspondence. The lower departure toward Laguna Colorada and the subsequent plain loop lack established through-links. An independent scholarly regional chapter corroborates the closed-basin lake setting but does not supply those links. This remains incomplete material correspondence rather than a completed name-scope hold.
records.supported_name_scope: El Barroso identifies the mapped northern Mapimí reach. It is not extended across the unnamed opening, Laguna Colorada passage or unestablished lower plain connectors.

scope_limits: El Barroso is a partial named reach, not a supported name for the full modeled system.
The named Boquilla de Acebuches and El Tordillo waterbodies are adjacent settings; no exact selected crossing is asserted.
Laguna Colorada has bounded lake-passage correspondence, but its approach and departure remain material gaps.
The actual terminal is not silently substituted with Las Liebres, Laguna de Tlahualilo or Laguna de Palomas.
Historical sources establish neither present water levels and operations nor perennial flow; those are not demanded as completion prerequisites.
The modeled length is not an official river length. Pinned selected positions were used for source orientation only and were not changed or revalidated.

records.region: Huancavelica and Ica; upper San Juan–Tantará–San Juan–Chico corridor, ending near Tambo de Mora
records.candidate_name_role: Provisional representative-system candidate with distinct upstream and managed downstream reach names
records.material_pending_reason: The chosen eastern opening and its connection into the Palmadera/upper San Juan course are not unambiguously distinguished in the inspected material. Detailed map P depicts several neighboring feeders, lakes and a proposed storage reach; the regional map and schematic do not establish which feeder carries the selected opening. Advertised base and hydrographic map pages are placeholders. This is a genuine selected-opening/through-link gap, not a demand for exact bank alignment.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Río San Juan identifies the connected main basin and substantial middle course. The selected route also uses an upper Palmadera/San Juan setting, a Tantará reach and the northern Chico outlet. The eastern opening is not securely assigned a feeder name or continuous source through-link.
records.completion_scope: All 34 parts were considered. The upper San Juan/Colcabamba joining setting, Tantará course, Huachos/Arma junction, main San Juan bends, lower Ayoque/Almacén context, Conta partition, northern Chico branch and Pacific terminal at Tambo de Mora are supported at ordinary corridor scale. The opening-to-Palmadera correspondence remains pending.
records.supported_name_scope: Reach and system context only; Río Chico is the selected northern coastward channel, distinct from the unselected Río Matagente outlet. No one hydronym is applied to every stored part.

scope_limits: The source shows several eastern headwater branches. None is imposed on the selected opening merely because it lies in the same upper basin.
The whole selected group combines differentiated named natural reaches with the source-described managed Chico outlet. A whole-feature natural-river scalar is not established.
The historical study establishes bounded map correspondence and naming context, not current hydraulic operation, present reservoir construction, exact banks or legal hydronym status.
Regional hydrographic description and detailed mapP do not substitute for missing selected-opening continuity.
The source cover and map dates differ within2003, and some source cartographic/prose labels are internally inconsistent; these are retained as source limitations rather than silently corrected.

bounded_name_observations.scope: Distinct selected upper-middle reach before the downstream San Juan name.

bounded_name_observations.scope: Selected northern managed lower channel from Conta partition to the Pacific at Tambo de Mora, distinct from Matagente.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
